record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral results from a parametrized directional-ablation weight edit, rather than reproducing the original activation-projection procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports a comparison table for harmful-prompt refusals and KL divergence on harmless prompts. Parameter-selection details and cited third-party benchmark results are not separate results of the claimed intervention; user comments are not study results.
record.test_reason: The README reports harmful-prompt refusal counts for Gemma 3 12B IT before and after difference-of-means weight-edit abliteration. That bears directly on V2: a weight edit removes refusal in a released model. The procedure is optimized, interpolated and component-weighted, so it is not a reproduction of V1's activation-level test. The repo is a backup copy of p-e-w/heretic, not original work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The README claims its automatic abliteration matches the refusal suppression of manual abliterations (3/100) at much lower KL divergence, which it reads as less capability damage.
record.recipe_differences: Uses first-token residual difference-of-means directions and directional ablation, but edits supported projection matrices with optimized, component-specific layer weights rather than applying the original activation projection at every layer and position. This repo presents a tool, not a stated reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablation weights vary by component and layer; the README says parameter optimization can improve the refusal/quality tradeoff, but does not report separate results by parameter setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Heretic's optimized abliteration gives lower KL divergence on harmless prompts (0.16) than other abliterations (0.45, 1.04), with equal refusal suppression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flexible, optimized ablation weight kernels reduce the distribution shift of abliteration at equal refusal removal.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to README-reported results for one displayed model and prompt set. The table gives no uncertainty or sample details for harmless prompts; KL divergence is only an indirect indicator of preserved capability. The code and evaluation were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows omitted. The README mentions independent MMLU and GSM8K benchmarking but points to external posts and gives no results for those benchmarks here.

untested.parts: Activation-level ablation at all layers and positions; inducing refusal by adding the direction; capability retention on benchmarks (MMLU/GSM8K mentioned only via external links).
Models other than Gemma 3 12B IT (other Heretic models are mentioned only through user comments); refusal judged by anything other than an automatic scorer.
All. Interpolated directions are a feature, not a tested comparison.
All. A gpt-oss-20b Heretic model exists, but only user comments are given.

record.verdict_notes: Tool README, not a study. It is a backup copy of p-e-w/heretic, so its results should be deduplicated with the original repo. Evidence is a single table with no uncertainty, an unclear refusal scorer, and possible overlap between optimization and evaluation prompts. The independent MMLU/GSM8K benchmarks are external Reddit links with no numbers given here. User testimonials are not results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce harmless-request refusals, projection at every layer and position, or general capability beyond KL divergence on harmless prompts.
The displayed comparison is for Gemma 3 12B IT; results for other released models are not reported in the table.
The README does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
The README describes interpolated directions as a feature, but does not report a result comparing one direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measures are reported.
No transfer results across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models are reported.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages is reported.
